question: A department has an AI policy but keeps no record of which connectors individual staff have linked to Claude. What is the greatest risk when a security incident review takes place?
options: A) Staff may duplicate one another's connections, creating extra work whenever a shared document is updated.
B) Nobody can establish what company data Claude could reach, so the review cannot scope the possible exposure.
C) Connectors left linked for long periods gradually slow down responses in conversations that do not use them.
D) The department may exceed the number of connections its plan permits and lose access without any warning.
correct_answers: B) Nobody can establish what company data Claude could reach, so the review cannot scope the possible exposure.
explanations: Duplicated connections are an efficiency annoyance rather than a barrier to understanding exposure.
Correct. Without an inventory the first question of any review, what data was reachable, cannot be answered, so the scope of the incident stays unknown.
Performance is not the governance concern, and it does not affect what a review is able to establish.
A capacity limit would be visible immediately and is unrelated to what an incident review needs to determine.
